title: introduce-ci-gatekeeper-and-lazy-dep-sync
author: Omar Kaminsky
description: Add a lightweight CI Gatekeeper service and a lazy dependency sync agent to reduce presubmit noise and speed feedback. Gatekeeper is a small Go binary that sits as a pre-merge policy check, performing deterministic rule evaluation (changelist size, dependency category, license flags) and making a pass/fail/soft-fail decision that can route PRs into fastpath lanes or require full presubmit lanes. The lazy dep sync agent defers expensive dependency resolution and lockfile churn to an async reconciler that populates a dep-snapshot artifact used by the presubmit fastpath to avoid reinstalling devdeps for trivial edits. This PR refactors existing presubmit wiring to a plugin model, migrates the presubmit workflow to a two-lane flow (fastpath vs full), introduces a small state machine for gate decisions, and adds operational observability (metrics and event logs). Motivation: long-running lint/test jobs caused noisy flakes and slow merges for low-risk PRs; repository-wide dependency churn from repeated lockfile updates increased CI time. Checklist: [x] gatekeeper service and config schema implemented, [x] presubmit router integrated into workflows, [x] lazy dep-sync agent implemented and reconciler cron job added, [x] metrics and traces added to Redwood observability-pack, [x] migration guide and docs/ci/fastpath.md, [x] smoke-tested on staging org. Rollout: staged rollout using feature flagging in presubmit router; enable fastpath for low-risk teams first, monitor errors for two days, then widen the cohort. Backout plan: disable presubmit fastpath flag and revert presubmit workflow to previous single-lane by removing the router step and dropping the gatekeeper check. Impact: reduces average presubmit runtime by up to 45% for trivial changes and decreases devdep rebuild frequency. See release_notes for more details.
commits: 6 commits: initial gatekeeper binary and schema; presubmit router integration; lazy dep-sync agent and reconciler; observability adapters and metrics; migration docs and feature-flag wiring; small follow-up fix for concurrency in dep-sync.
review_comments: Asha: The gate decision logic is compact but please add an explicit unit test for license-blocking rules (we had a regression last quarter).
Omar: Added license rule unit tests and a small e2e that runs gatekeeper against a sample manifest (see ci/testdata).

Michael: Two nits on logging levels and an edge-case in the reconciler when network is flaky; recommend retry backoff. Omar: addressed the logging nits and added an exponential backoff with jitter in the reconciler (last commit).
Lena: Approving after smoke runs on staging. Left a suggestion to add a dashboard tile for fastpath ratio — will follow up in a separate PR.
release_notes: Introduces a presubmit gatekeeper that routes low-risk PRs to a fastpath and adds a lazy dependency sync to reduce devdep rebuilds. Admins can toggle fastpath via feature flags. Expect faster presubmit feedback for non-dep-touching changes and less lockfile churn. See docs/ci/fastpath.md for migration steps.
risk_assessment: medium: changes presubmit gating behavior and affects CI routing; rollout behind feature flag, easy rollback path documented.
backout_plan: Disable presubmit router feature flag and revert .github/workflows/presubmit.yml to previous commit; gatekeeper binary can be disabled via config and reconciler cronjob disabled. Detailed rollback steps are in docs/ci/migration.md.
notes_for_ops: Prometheus metrics added: presubmit_gate_decisions_total, presubmit_fastpath_ratio, dep_sync_reconcile_duration_seconds. Alert if fastpath success rate drops below 90% or reconciler error rate spikes. Reconciler runs every 30m by default; tune via CI_DEP_SYNC_CRON env.
why_this_is_unique: Instead of only trimming CI matrix sizes or moving tests, this PR adds a policy-driven gate + lazy dep sync to reduce both noise and rebuild cost. The presubmit router is extensible for future risk heuristics (author tenure, churn delta) and avoids lockfile thrash by reconciling deps asynchronously.
